samples.summary: Customer-facing REST docs still describe the pre-change contract for merges and freeze: no mention of the new 409 on `PUT merges` (straddling the freeze), the two new 400 caps (`MaxMergeEntries` 10,000 entries, `MaxMergeCoveredCells` 1,000,000 covered cells), the freeze-straddle 409 on `POST move`, or that `PUT freeze` may store (and return) a boundary deeper than the one requested.
samples.evidence: packages/documentation/developers/rest-api.md:693 lists only `rs * cs` ≤ 100,000 as a merge rule; :653 documents the freeze pair with no snapping; :563 and :631 list the move 409 as "merge split" only. The diff adds `assertMergesClearOfFreeze`, `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze`, `mergeBudgetError` in `parseMerges` and `snapFreezePastMerges` in `setFreeze` without touching this file.

samples.summary: Design doc for the v1 API states "Each endpoint echoes back the request it applied" and lists only the merge-split 409; `PUT freeze` can now echo a snapped boundary, `PUT merges` can 409, and `POST move` can 409 on a freeze straddle.
samples.evidence: docs/design/rest-api.md:278 (echo claim) and :314 ("A move that would split a merged range returns 409" as the only merge refusal) were not updated by this change.

samples.summary: The frontend store-contract table describes `setMerge(anchor, span)` as an unconditional write to `root.sheets[tabId].merges[anchorSref]`; it is now budgeted and can refuse, returning `false` without writing.
samples.evidence: docs/design/frontend.md:291 — `| setMerge(anchor, span) | Write to root.sheets[tabId].merges[anchorSref] |`, unchanged while `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:1008` gained the budget refusal.

samples.summary: `ReadOnlyStore.setMerge` now returns `false`, so `Sheet.mergeSelection` returns early and no longer updates the in-memory merge map for read-only-backed sheets; datasource and lakehouse views lose the local-only merge they previously rendered.
samples.evidence: Consumers: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/datasource-view.tsx:29 and packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/lakehouse-view.tsx:40 construct `new ReadOnlyStore()`; the early return is at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4969, ahead of `this.merges.set(...)` at :4985. Same applies to `applyPasteMerges` (sheet.ts:2770).

samples.summary: The legacy-shape migration copies `merges` and `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` verbatim into the new worksheet shape, bypassing both new guards: no `snapFreezePastMerges` and no merge-budget check, so it can install exactly the straddling / over-budget map the change claims only a raw CRDT writer can create.
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-shape-migration.ts:444 `merges: cloneMergeRecord(legacy.merges)` and :449-450 `frozenRows/frozenCols: legacy.frozenRows ?? 0`. The same class of unguarded copy exists in packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.ts and packages/backend/src/template/seed/seed-templates.ts:140.

samples.summary: The concurrency test driver ignores the new boolean from `moveRows`/`moveColumns`; a move now silently refused on one replica (split merge or merge landing across a freeze) makes the two replicas diverge with no signal, which shows up as an opaque convergence failure rather than a skipped op.
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/test/helpers/concurrency-driver.ts:52-56 `await sheet.moveRows(op.src, op.count, op.dst); return;` — the refusal path added at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1596 is invisible here.

samples.summary: After `store.shiftCells` has already snapped the freeze inside the CRDT (via `applyWorksheetShift`), `Sheet.shiftCells` recomputes the snap from its own in-memory merge map and writes it back with `store.setFreezePane`. Because `rebuildMergeCoverMap` now *drops* over-budget/malformed entries from `this.merges`, the local map can be a strict subset of the stored one, so the second write can overwrite the store's correct boundary with a shallower one.
samples.evidence: Writer: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1471-1483; the independent snap in the doc is at packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:278 (reached from packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:487). The pruning that can make the two maps differ is sheet.ts:914 `this.merges = admitted`.

samples.summary: Visual-harness scenarios write the freeze pane straight through `MemStore.setFreezePane`, bypassing `Sheet.setFreezePane`'s new snap; a scenario that later gains a merge across that boundary would baseline the state the change declares undrawable.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/harness/visual/sheet-scenarios.tsx:117 `await store.setFreezePane(1, 1);` and :333 `await store.setFreezePane(2, 0);` (merge scenario at :230 uses a separate store, so nothing straddles today).

finding.summary: New freeze-snap can grow frozenRows/frozenCols without bound; the renderer paints every frozen row/column per frame
finding.evidence:
`snapFreezePastMerges` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/merging.ts) grows the freeze line to the far edge of any merged block it would cut, and it is now applied from `Sheet.setFreezePane` (sheet.ts:543), `Sheet.shiftCells` (sheet.ts:1432), `applyWorksheetShift` (worksheet-structure.ts:278) and the backend `PUT .../freeze` (worksheet.controller.ts:118). The merge budget explicitly permits a single span of `MaxMergedCells` = 100,000 cells, e.g. `A2:A100001` (`canMergeSelection` only rejects a span over that cap), so freezing row 2 above such a block silently stores `frozenRows = 100001`.

The consumer that was not considered is the renderer: `GridCanvas.render` paints the frozen quadrant with `renderQuadrantCells(ctx, 1, fr + 1, ...)` (packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:329-332) — the loop runs over every frozen row each frame with no viewport culling (the `ctx.clip()` only clips pixels), and `buildFreezeState` (view/layout.ts:149) computes `frozenHeight = rowDim.getOffset(frozenRows + 1)`, which for such a value exceeds the viewport and makes quadrant D's rect (gridcanvas.ts:282-287) degenerate. This is exactly the failure `parseFreeze`'s own doc says its bound exists to prevent (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:53-56: "the frozen quadrants render every frozen row and column without viewport clipping, so an out-of-grid freeze allocates per frame and the UI never paints") — and the snap reaches it from an in-bounds request, both in the editor and through the v1 API. Fix belongs on the new snap (cap it, or refuse the freeze instead of snapping past a very large block).

verdict.reason: The finding's core claim — that `snapFreezePastMerges` grows the freeze line without bound and can silently store `frozenRows = 100001` — is not present in the code. The sweep is explicitly capped: `if (snapped !== line && snapped > MaxSnappedFreeze) return 0;` (merging.ts:361), with `MaxSnappedFreeze = 1000` (merging.ts:60) documented at merging.ts:44-59 for precisely the renderer reason cited (frozen quadrants painted in full each frame). Freezing row 2 above an `A2:A100001` merge therefore releases the axis to 0, not 100001. All four named entry points call this same capped implementation rather than a copy: Sheet.setFreezePane (sheet.ts:544 -> 557-562), Sheet.shiftCells (sheet.ts:1472), applyWorksheetShift (worksheet-structure.ts:278, importing from merging.ts at line 18), and the v1 controller (worksheet.controller.ts:121, importing from the sheets package at line 15, after parseFreeze bounds the request at worksheet-settings.ts:58-63). Tests assert the release behaviour (merge.test.ts:998-1009, 1023-1031). The only way a large frozenRows survives is an explicitly requested line with no merge growth (merge.test.ts:1011-1021), which is the request-validation path, not the snap the finding targets.
